significance: A hilltop shrine at Chobhar to one of the four Lokeshwars of the Kathmandu valley, revered by Buddhists and Hindus alike; built in the 15th century and rebuilt in 1640. Visitors know it for the pots, pans and other household vessels nailed across its walls as offerings.
story: The image is said to have been fished out of the river by Suval Acharya and installed on Kacchapala hill, where an annual bathing rite was founded for it.
